mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 0.5% coincident with a flattening industrial production trend (INDPRO) predicts weakening corporate revenue growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -0.5% AND INDPRO flat for 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the correlation between GDPC1 decline and negative returns drops below 0.3.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% for three consecutive months, combined with rising payrolls (PAYEMS), signals a tight labor market that pressures firms to raise wages and prices, compressing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0% for 3 consecutive months AND PAYEMS rising
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for two consecutive months, absent a similar decline in consumption (GDPC1), indicates supply-side disruptions that raise input costs and reduce profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < -0.5% for 2 consecutive months AND GDPC1 flat
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% signals a housing market recovery, boosting construction-related equities and contributing to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of strong HOUST outperformance.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.75 percentage points signals an emergency easing, lowering risk-free rates and boosting risk asset valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive after such an FEDFUNDS drop.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid deceleration in payrolls growth (PAYEMS) to below 50,000 new jobs per month for two consecutive months, while unemployment rises, signals labor market weakening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < 50,000 for 2 consecutive months AND UNRATE rising
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) of more than 3% coincident with rising retail sales (RSAFS) predicts continued consumer strength and positive corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY > 3% AND RSAFS rising for 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during such consumption booms.
